div.head: II Cn 68.3
div.ab: ⁊ gyf hwa hwæt ungewealdes gedeð, ne byð þæt eallunga na gelíc, þe hit gewealdes gewurþe.
And gif hwa ungewealdes gedeð, ne bið þæt eallum na gelic, þe hit gewealdes gedeð.
Et si quisquam agat aliquid inpossibiliter, non est omnino simile, si uoluntarie faciat.
And gyf hwa ungewealdes hwæt gedeð, ne byð þæt eallunga gelíc ðam ðe hit gewealdes deð.
And gyf hwa hwæt ungewealdes gedeð, ne byð þæt eallunga na gelic þe hit gewealdes gedeð.
And if anyone does anything unintentionally, the case is entirely different from that of one who acts deliberately.
And if anyone does something unintentionally, then it is not to be treated in any way as if the act were carried out with intent.
And if anyone does anything unintentionally, it is not at all the same as if it happened by intention.
Und wenn einer etwas unabsichtlich verübt, ist das nicht gänzlich gleich (dem B), der es absichtlich verübt (dass es a. geschieht G).
And if anyone does something unintentionally, that is not wholly the same as (as the one, B) who does it intentionally (as its happening intentionally, G).
div.note: A and Ld read ‘gedeð’ for G's ‘gewurþe’, which Liebermann thinks more original (the Canons of Edgar have ‘misdeð’). Liebermann compares Canons of Edgar, Confessional 4.
